frequency_question: How often does the Department of Education formally revoke an accrediting agency's recognition within a given review cycle?
membership_rule: Includes all formal administrative proceedings by the U.S. Department of Education regarding the renewal, limitation, suspension, or revocation of nationally recognized accrediting agencies.
window: Multi-year review and renewal windows spanning 1990 to present.

cases.name: American College of Financial Services review
Accrediting Council for Independent Colleges and Schools (ACICS) 2016 action
ACICS reinstatement and final revocation action
American Bar Association periodic review cycles (multiple instances)
National Academy of Early Childhood Programs accreditation review

provenance_note: claims 120 cases from only 5 named (24.0x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 5 named key historical enforcement actions and cycles; estimated ~120 total major institutional review instances across the historical window.
known_gaps: Excludes minor compliance warnings, stipulations, and secretarial defundings that did not culminate in final formal recognition revocation.
skeleton: Total major national accrediting agencies evaluated in formal periodic review cycles resulting in severe adverse recognition outcomes.
multiplier: Approximately 45 major recognized accrediting bodies reviewed on 5-to-10 year cycles over 30 years, yielding roughly 120 total review instances, with 3 full terminations.
validity_reason: Administrative review standards and statutory oversight criteria for accrediting agencies remain stable across multiple presidential administrations.
